title: Refrigeration, ice and coffee machines: the cleaning boundary
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Ozone Protection and Synthetic Greenhouse Gas Management Regulations 1995 (compilation dated 9 February 2018, an older version). The refrigerant licence offence in regulation 111 has only been partly confirmed.
audience: Workers who clean the outside and accessible drip and bin areas of ice machines, coffee machines, refrigerated display units and similar appliances
learningOutcomes: Identify the refrigerant circuit and water-carrying parts that are outside the cleaning scope
Clean the accessible drip tray, grounds bin, bin lid, door seal and exterior of an ice or coffee machine
Explain why refrigerant handling and refrigeration circuit work need a refrigerant handling licence
Record and refer a water, drain or refrigeration fault without attempting a repair

instruction.heading: What sits inside the refrigeration boundary
instruction.body: Ice machines, coffee machines with refrigerated milk units, and refrigerated display cabinets contain a refrigerant circuit made of a compressor, a condenser, an expansion device and an evaporator. The circuit is sealed, and it is the part of the machine that carries refrigerant gas. Water-carrying parts include the water inlet valve, the inlet filter, the water distribution system, the evaporator plate or bin on an ice machine, the boiler or heating element of a coffee machine, and the internal water lines. These parts are outside this course. In practice, the cleaning boundary is the outside of the cabinet, the door and door seal, the accessible drip tray and grounds bin, the bin lid and its outside surface, and the exterior of the condenser grille where it is accessible without tools. Until the business compliance record confirms the position, treat the coil as outside the scope, record it, and refer it.

instruction.heading: Why refrigerant work is a licensed task
instruction.body: Regulation 111 makes it an offence to carry out work on RAC equipment without a licence (2018 compilation; check the current version). That work includes any act with refrigerant, or with a component that carries a risk of refrigerant escaping, and the regulation reaches decommissioning where refrigerant is in the equipment. A cleaner who opens a refrigeration housing, disturbs a pipe, or touches the compressor, the condenser coil or a service valve is doing work that may need the licence, and this course does not grant it. Refrigerant can cause frostbite on contact, and some refrigerants are flammable, so a leak is a hazard in its own right, not just a loss of cooling.

instruction.heading: Water, drain and bin areas: clean, check, refer
instruction.body: The drip tray, grounds bin and ice bin are the most cleaned parts of these machines, and they hold water and food residue, so they need regular wiping. Empty the drip tray and bin into the approved waste container, rinse with clean water, and dry before refitting. Check the drain outlet for blockage without inserting tools into the internal drain line. If water is leaking, if the drain is blocked, if the water inlet appears to be leaking, or if the machine makes a new sound, stop cleaning around that part and record it. Do not reset the machine, do not remove the water inlet filter, and do not open the cabinet. Ice machines and coffee machines can have hot or very cold surfaces, and some have a water supply under pressure, so isolate the machine as set out in lesson “Making a machine safe before cleaning: isolation, stored energy and moving parts” before you clean near its water connections.

procedure: Confirm the machine is isolated under “Making a machine safe before cleaning: isolation, stored energy and moving parts” before cleaning near water connections, drain outlets or the bin area.
Record the refrigeration boundary for the job, and mark the condenser coil, refrigerant circuit and internal water parts as excluded.
Remove the bin contents and drip tray into the approved waste container, following the site waste procedure.
Clean the drip tray, grounds bin, ice bin exterior, bin lid, door seal and cabinet exterior with the approved product and a damp cloth.
Check the drain outlet from outside for blockage, and do not insert tools into the internal drain line.
Dry the tray and bin and refit them, then confirm the machine is secure and the drip tray is seated.
If you see water leaking, a blocked drain, a frozen or warm surface, or a new noise, stop, record it, and refer to the owner's service provider.
Record the boundary, the parts cleaned, the parts excluded and any referral made.

workedExamples.situation: You are asked to clean an ice machine including its condenser grille, which is at the back. The grille is dusty and the booking says the machine must be left clean for inspection.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you clean the condenser coil?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not clean it with water or tools. Clean the accessible outside of the cabinet, the bin and the door seal. Record the coil as excluded, with a photograph, and refer it to the owner's refrigeration provider. Do not touch the compressor or any pipe.

workedExamples.situation: A coffee machine's drip tray is full of water and the water is coming from an inlet connection at the back. The owner says the inlet filter has been blocked for a while and asks you to change it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you change the inlet filter?
workedExamples.reasoning: The inlet filter is on the water supply and is part of the internal water system. Changing it is outside this course. Isolate the machine as in “Making a machine safe before cleaning: isolation, stored energy and moving parts” if you can do so safely, dry the tray, record the leak and the owner's request with photographs, and refer the inlet to the owner's service provider. Do not change the filter, and do not reset the machine.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves suitable for cold surfaces and the approved product
Approved waste container and bin liners for ice and grounds
Eye protection for splashes from drip trays and drain outlets

commonErrors.error: Cleaning the condenser coil with a brush, water or compressed air because it looks dusty.
commonErrors.prevention: Treat the coil as excluded until the compliance record confirms the boundary. Record and refer it.

commonErrors.error: Changing the water inlet filter to stop a leak, without isolation or authority.
commonErrors.prevention: The inlet is internal water work and is excluded. Isolate if safe, record, and refer.

commonErrors.error: Inserting a tool into the drain line to clear a blockage.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the drain outlet from outside only. Refer any blockage that needs internal access.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Refrigerant handling and work on refrigeration circuits require a refrigerant handling licence under regulation 111 (2018 compilation; check the current version). This lesson does not grant that licence.
Until it is confirmed, the coil is excluded.
The worker must not change inlet filters, fittings or drain lines under this course.

qualityStandard: The refrigeration boundary is recorded before cleaning, with the coil and internal water parts marked excluded
The drip tray, bin and cabinet exterior are clean, dry and seated correctly
No internal refrigeration or water part is opened, adjusted or cleaned
documentationEvidence: The refrigeration and water boundary record, with photographs of the excluded parts
The waste disposal record for the bin and drip tray contents
Any leak, blockage or abnormal noise, with the referral made
summary: The refrigerant circuit and internal water parts are outside this course.
Clean the accessible cabinet exterior, drip tray, bin, bin lid and door seal, and check the drain outlet from outside.
Record and refer any leak, blockage or suspected refrigerant issue, and do not reset or repair.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an ice machine is part of the refrigerant circuit and is outside this course?
options: The outside of the cabinet
The bin lid and its hinge
The door seal and gasket
The compressor and its pipes

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the Commonwealth refrigerant rules, what licence must a person hold to carry out work on refrigeration equipment?
options: A refrigerant handling licence
A general building licence
A food handler certificate
A manufacturer's warranty card

knowledgeChecks.question: The drip tray of a coffee machine is leaking because the water inlet filter is blocked. What is the correct response?
options: Change the filter so the machine works again, since the inlet is simply blocked and easy to fix
Dry the tray, isolate if safe, record the leak with photographs, and refer the inlet to the service provider
Reset the machine and see if the leak stops, since the fault may clear on its own after a short wait
Drill a hole in the tray to drain it properly, so the water leaves the machine and nothing pools below

knowledgeChecks.question: How should the drain outlet of an ice machine be checked during a clean?
options: By inserting a tool into the internal drain line to clear any blockage
By removing the back panel to check the drain from inside
From outside only, with no tools inserted into the internal line
By pouring hot water into the bin until it runs out of the outlet

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is refrigerant a hazard in its own right, not just a cooling issue?
options: Refrigerant is harmless to touch when it is not under pressure at all
Refrigerant only affects the colour of the machine and its finish
Refrigerant is only a problem in outdoor machines that face the weather
Refrigerant can cause frostbite on contact, and some types are flammable
